newsitem.title: RUSSIA: No chance of cancelling Yeltsin op - top doctor.
newsitem.headline: No chance of cancelling Yeltsin op - top doctor.

text.p: The top Russian surgeon who is expected to lead President Boris Yeltsin's planned heart operation said on Tuesday that there was no chance of the surgery being cancelled.
Asked by reporters if it was possible that the operation could be cancelled, Renat Akchurin replied simply: "No."
Akchurin made several statements over the weekend which fuelled speculation about the real state of health of the 65-year-old Russian leader.
Yeltsin disappeared from the public eye in late June and said on September 5 he had decided to undergo an operation to be able to return to active life.

Akchurin said Yeltsin could have suffered a third, unreported heart attack between the two rounds of the Russian presidential election, about the same time when he retreated from public life. Yeltsin had two mild heart attacks last year.
Akchurin also said that the operation, which Yeltsin had said was expected at the end of September, could be postponed for up to eight weeks in order to prepare the patient.
